newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - March 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - March 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh's High Court on Sunday asked the government to show cause in seven days why the detention of the four top opposition leaders be declared illegal.
Expansion of bilateral economic and cultural coopration will be the focus at the official talks during the visit of Turkish President Suleyman Demirel due in Dhaka on Tuesday.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina called upon the OIC nations who have surplus resources to invest those within the Islamic world for meaningful cooperation under the fold of the forum.

Turkish President Suleyman Demirel, South African President Nelson Mandela and Palestinian leader Yaser Araft will arrive in Dhaka on Tuesday to participate in the independence day celebration on Wednesday.
Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) chief Begum Khaleda Zia has warned the government that any repressive policy would "hasten" its fall.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Sunday proposed a seven-point plan of action at a OIC summit in Islamabad for promotion of solidarity and cooperation among the Islamic countries.
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is likely to finance a $70 million project for development of the country's capital market.

An agreement between the local Jamuna Oil Company Ltd and the Mobil Asia Pacific Ltd of the United States on a joint venture plant to produce LP gas and lubricant oil is expected to be signed in April. REUTER
